claims.text: High-entropy alloys can exhibit significant local atomic-scale disorder.
Local coordination environments and bond-length distributions can serve as descriptors of local atomic configuration disorder.
Local lattice distortions and chemical disorder enhance phonon scattering.
Increased atomic-scale disorder disrupts phonon propagation.
Disruption of phonon propagation by atomic-scale disorder reduces phonon thermal conductivity.
Explicitly incorporating disorder-related structural descriptors will represent disorder-mediated phonon scattering more accurately than models based on averaged properties.
A predictive approach incorporating local atomic configuration disorder will outperform current models in identifying high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach will reduce prediction error relative to experiment by approximately 10–20% compared with conventional models.
High-entropy alloys selected for high local-disorder metrics will have lower phonon thermal conductivity.
Current prediction models largely use averaged compositional and crystallographic data without detailed resolution of local atomic environments.
The predictive improvement will be significant primarily in high-entropy alloy systems where local atomic-scale disorder predominates.
The proposed approach may not improve accuracy in systems with minimal local lattice distortion.
The proposed approach may not improve accuracy when heat-transport mechanisms other than disorder-mediated phonon transport dominate.
Synthesis and measurement variability can affect the quantitative improvement in prediction accuracy.
Local atomic disorder is challenging to quantify experimentally with sufficient accuracy.
A failure to obtain a statistically significant prediction-error reduction relative to conventional models would falsify the hypothesis.
A failure to observe the predicted association between quantified local disorder and reduced phonon thermal conductivity would falsify the hypothesis.
